subject: MedWorks pilot: model-improvement prohibition & prompt/response ownership
messages:
From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@medworks.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medworks.com>
Date: 2025-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot contract ask — prohibition on model improvement & ownership of prompts/responses

Hi Vivek / David,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the team at MedWorks is excited to start the small pilot. Before we spin up test traffic Procurement flagged two items we need contract language for:

1) A clear prohibition on using customer pilot data to improve or further train any model (including internal tuning/benchmarks).
2) Confirmation that prompts we send and the exact generated responses from the model are treated as customer-owned and not used for derivatives beyond the pilot.

We attached a short DPA excerpt with our suggested redlines (MedWorks_DPA_redline_v1.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these constraints for a pilot (no model-learning, ephemeral retention, and prompt/response ownership)? Also please advise what operational controls you’ll need from us (sampling, telemetry toggles, log retention).

If you prefer, Procurement can route a redline to your legal — I'll attach the current doc. Hoping to finalize by next week so we can kick off.

Appreciate it,
Alex Greene
Head of Engineering Programs
MedWorks Health

Attachment: MedWorks_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@medworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract ask — prohibition on model improvement & ownership of prompts/responses

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the redline. We're glad MedWorks wants to run the pilot. High-level answers up front: yes, we can support a pilot with a learning-prohibition and customer ownership of prompts/responses, but we’ll need to lock operational guardrails and a short evidence workflow.

Practical items we need from you:
- Confirm the pilot scope (number of users, peak RPS, types of data that might contain PHI).
- Which endpoints will be in scope (chat, completion, embeddings).
- Whether you require onshore (US) residency or any encryption-by-customer-key (KMS).

Operational controls we propose for the pilot (we can include as implementation appendix in the DPA):
- Ephemeral prompt retention: prompts and responses deleted from runtime logs after 72 hours unless explicitly flagged for debugging (flagging must be agreed and timeboxed).
- Telemetry: we can disable full-text telemetry for the pilot; only anonymized performance metrics will be retained.
- No-model-improvement: we will create a project-level marker that prevents your traffic from being used in any internal tuning datasets; we will also prevent routing to any experimental model variants that rely on customer data.

I'll loop Marissa (legal/product counsel) and David (ops) to propose contractual language and the ops checklist. If you can share the procurement contact and desired timeline we’ll prioritize the redline review.

— Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@medworks.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medworks.com>
Date: 2025-05-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract ask — prohibition on model improvement & ownership of prompts/responses

Thanks Vivek — that plan helps. Pilot scope: 3 internal teams, up to 20 concurrent users, using chat and completion endpoints. Data will include de-identified clinical summaries (we will not send raw PHI). Residency: US only. KMS: not required for pilot.

Procurement is the main contact — procurement@medworks.com. Target timeline: sign DPA by 2025-06-05 and begin pilot the week of 2025-06-09.

I've attached an updated redline and a short requirements doc. We can accept an evidence workflow where Redwood provides an operational runbook and a one-time attestation that the traffic was excluded from training.

Attachment: MedWorks_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (updated)
Attachment: MedWorks_summary_requirements.docx

Alex

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@medworks.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-01T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract ask — prohibition on model improvement & ownership of prompts/responses

Alex — quick operational notes on how we will implement the guardrails so your security team can validate:

1) Data flow: requests hit our routing tier and are tagged with a "no-learn" project label. Tagged requests are excluded from any async logging pipelines used for model improvement.
2) KV/Prefix caching: we will disable cross-customer reuse and mark any per-session KV as ephemeral; keys will be evicted once session ends.
3) Runtime logs: we can configure 72-hour retention and automatic purge by project ID. If you require a shorter retention we can do 24 hours for the pilot.
4) Evidence: after the pilot we will provide:
   - a signed attestation stating the traffic was not included in any training/tuning datasets;
   - an operations runbook snapshot showing retention/KV/toggle settings;
   - a CSV extract (redacted) of service-level events verifying project labels for a sample period.

Operational caveat: for debug sessions where MedWorks requests a saved transcript, we'll require explicit manual approval and local retention will be timeboxed and audited.

Let us know if 72 hours retention + signed attestation meet your procurement needs. Happy to tighten retention to 24 hours if required for the contract.

— David Kim
Director, Reliability & Security
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@medworks.com>, procurement@medworks.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract ask — prohibition on model improvement & ownership of prompts/responses

Alex / Procurement,

Following up with proposed contract language snippets we can accept for the pilot. Below are two short clauses — feel free to paste into your redline and we will review any edits.

1) No Model Improvement
"During the term of the Pilot, Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, inputs, outputs, or derived logs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models or model parameters. For the avoidance of doubt, Customer Data shall be excluded from any datasets or processes used for model evaluation, tuning, or experimentation."

2) Prompt & Response Ownership and Ephemeral Retention
"Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data, including prompts and the outputs generated in response. Redwood agrees to retain Customer Data in production logs only for a maximum of seventy-two (72) hours, after which such data will be automatically deleted, except where Customer explicitly requests retention for debugging (each request must be documented and timeboxed). Redwood will provide a one-time attestation following the Pilot that Customer Data was not used for model training or improvement."

If those clauses look good, we will accept a counter-redline and prepare the attestation template (we can include the runbook as an appendix). If you need additional onshore or KMS constraints for later phases, we can scope those into Dedicated/Private deployment discussions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Product
Redwood Inference
